---
title: "Niche similarity and spatial co-occurrence: Mantel and bipartite QAP analyses"
author: "Gómez-Vadillo, Mónica"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 2
---

The analysis uses only the 2,317 unique `ET_ID` values in the study-area layer. Climatic distance is `1 - Jaccard` and co-occurrence is the absolute number of shared 50-km cells. The within-group tests are Pearson Mantel tests; the intergroup test uses a bipartite QAP permutation design.

For the within-group tests, the negative one-sided permutation probability is calculated from the lower tail of the Mantel permutation distribution. The intergroup test uses only the 84 × 35 Lentic–Lotic comparisons. Its null distribution independently permutes species labels within each group, preserving the bipartite pair structure and the reuse of each species across pairs.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(readxl)
library(vegan)
library(knitr)

permutations <- 9999L
seed_base <- 20261014L
analysis_root <- "01_Data/04_Data_Analysis"

required_files <- c(
  "01_Data/04_Data_Analysis/01_Lentic/MJacc_lentic.csv",
  "01_Data/04_Data_Analysis/02_Lotic/MJacc_lotic.csv",
  "01_Data/04_Data_Analysis/03_LenticVSLotic/MJacc_LenticVSLotic.csv",
  file.path(analysis_root, "01_Lentic/lentic_lentic_cooccurrence.csv"),
  file.path(analysis_root, "02_Lotic/lotic_lotic_cooccurrence.csv"),
  file.path(analysis_root, "03_LenticVSLotic/intergroup_cooccurrence.csv")
)
missing_files <- required_files[!file.exists(required_files)]
if (length(missing_files) > 0) {
  stop("Missing required inputs; run 05_Coocurrence.R first: ",
       paste(missing_files, collapse = ", "))
}

species_group <- as.data.frame(read_excel(
  "01_Data/03_Data_species/List_of_species.xlsx",
  sheet = "species_group"
))
lentic_species <- as.character(species_group$species[species_group$group == "Lentic"])
lotic_species <- as.character(species_group$species[species_group$group == "Lotic"])
lentic_species <- setdiff(lentic_species, c("sp_14", "sp_67", "sp_91"))
lotic_species <- setdiff(lotic_species, c("sp_21", "sp_124"))
all_species <- c(lentic_species, lotic_species)

if (length(lentic_species) != 84L || length(lotic_species) != 35L ||
    anyDuplicated(all_species)) {
  stop("Species groups do not match the expected 84 lentic and 35 lotic species.")
}

read_jaccard <- function(path) {
  matrix <- as.matrix(read.csv(path, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
  storage.mode(matrix) <- "numeric"
  if (nrow(matrix) != ncol(matrix) ||
      !setequal(rownames(matrix), colnames(matrix)) ||
      anyNA(matrix) || any(matrix < 0 | matrix > 1)) {
    stop("Invalid Jaccard matrix: ", path)
  }
  matrix[rownames(matrix), rownames(matrix), drop = FALSE]
}

make_square_cooccurrence <- function(pairs, species, require_complete = TRUE) {
  if (!all(c("sp1", "sp2", "cooccurrence_cells") %in% names(pairs)) ||
      anyNA(pairs[, c("sp1", "sp2", "cooccurrence_cells")])) {
    stop("Invalid co-occurrence pair table.")
  }
  sp1 <- as.character(pairs$sp1)
  sp2 <- as.character(pairs$sp2)
  pair_key <- paste(pmin(sp1, sp2), pmax(sp1, sp2), sep = "|")
  if (anyDuplicated(pair_key) || any(!sp1 %in% species) || any(!sp2 %in% species)) {
    stop("Duplicate pairs or species outside the declared group in pair table.")
  }
  expected <- choose(length(species), 2)
  if (require_complete && nrow(pairs) != expected) {
    stop("Incomplete within-group co-occurrence table.")
  }

  result <- matrix(0, length(species), length(species),
                   dimnames = list(species, species))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(pairs))) {
    result[sp1[i], sp2[i]] <- pairs$cooccurrence_cells[i]
    result[sp2[i], sp1[i]] <- pairs$cooccurrence_cells[i]
  }
  result
}

run_intragroup_mantel <- function(jaccard, cooccurrence, seed) {
  if (!identical(rownames(jaccard), colnames(jaccard)) ||
      !identical(dimnames(jaccard), dimnames(cooccurrence)) ||
      nrow(jaccard) < 3L) {
    stop("Jaccard and co-occurrence matrices are not identically aligned.")
  }
  set.seed(seed)
  result <- vegan::mantel(
    as.dist(cooccurrence),
    as.dist(1 - jaccard),
    method = "pearson",
    permutations = permutations
  )
  permutation_statistics <- result$perm
  p_negative <- (sum(permutation_statistics <= result$statistic) + 1) /
    (length(permutation_statistics) + 1)
  list(
    r = unname(result$statistic),
    p_default_upper = unname(result$signif),
    p_negative = p_negative,
    n_pairs = choose(nrow(jaccard), 2)
  )
}
```

## Within-group tests

```{r within-group}
jaccard_lentic <- read_jaccard(
  "01_Data/04_Data_Analysis/01_Lentic/MJacc_lentic.csv"
)
jaccard_lotic <- read_jaccard(
  "01_Data/04_Data_Analysis/02_Lotic/MJacc_lotic.csv"
)
if (!setequal(rownames(jaccard_lentic), lentic_species) ||
    !setequal(rownames(jaccard_lotic), lotic_species)) {
  stop("Within-group Jaccard species do not match the species catalogue.")
}
jaccard_lentic <- jaccard_lentic[lentic_species, lentic_species, drop = FALSE]
jaccard_lotic <- jaccard_lotic[lotic_species, lotic_species, drop = FALSE]

lentic_pairs <- read.csv(
  file.path(analysis_root, "01_Lentic/lentic_lentic_cooccurrence.csv")
)
lotic_pairs <- read.csv(
  file.path(analysis_root, "02_Lotic/lotic_lotic_cooccurrence.csv")
)
lentic_result <- run_intragroup_mantel(
  jaccard_lentic,
  make_square_cooccurrence(lentic_pairs, lentic_species),
  seed_base
)
lotic_result <- run_intragroup_mantel(
  jaccard_lotic,
  make_square_cooccurrence(lotic_pairs, lotic_species),
  seed_base + 1L
)

data.frame(
  group = c("Lentic-Lentic", "Lotic-Lotic"),
  test = "Pearson Mantel, one-sided negative",
  r = c(lentic_result$r, lotic_result$r),
  p = c(lentic_result$p_negative, lotic_result$p_negative),
  n_pairs = c(lentic_result$n_pairs, lotic_result$n_pairs)
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 5)
```

The Mantel test permutes one square species-distance matrix while retaining the shared-species structure. The p-value is the lower-tail proportion for the prespecified negative association, with the plus-one correction.

## Intergroup test

```{r intergroup}
jaccard_all <- read_jaccard(
  "01_Data/04_Data_Analysis/03_LenticVSLotic/MJacc_LenticVSLotic.csv"
)
if (!setequal(rownames(jaccard_all), all_species)) {
  stop("Intergroup Jaccard matrix does not match the species catalogue.")
}
jaccard_all <- jaccard_all[all_species, all_species, drop = FALSE]

inter_pairs <- read.csv(
  file.path(analysis_root, "03_LenticVSLotic/intergroup_cooccurrence.csv")
)
if (nrow(inter_pairs) != length(lentic_species) * length(lotic_species)) {
  stop("Intergroup tables must contain every Lentic-Lotic pair exactly once.")
}

make_rectangular_cooccurrence <- function(pairs, rows, columns) {
  result <- matrix(NA_real_, length(rows), length(columns),
                   dimnames = list(rows, columns))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(pairs))) {
    row_species <- as.character(pairs$sp1[i])
    column_species <- as.character(pairs$sp2[i])
    if (!row_species %in% rows || !column_species %in% columns ||
        !is.na(result[row_species, column_species])) {
      stop("Unexpected or duplicate Lentic-Lotic pair.")
    }
    result[row_species, column_species] <- pairs$cooccurrence_cells[i]
  }
  if (anyNA(result)) {
    stop("The rectangular matrix is missing one or more observed pairs.")
  }
  result
}

jaccard_cross <- jaccard_all[lentic_species, lotic_species, drop = FALSE]
cooccurrence_cross <- make_rectangular_cooccurrence(
  inter_pairs,
  lentic_species,
  lotic_species
)
if (!identical(dimnames(jaccard_cross), dimnames(cooccurrence_cross))) {
  stop("Rectangular intergroup matrices are not identically aligned.")
}

bipartite_mantel <- function(jaccard, cooccurrence, seed) {
  distance <- 1 - jaccard
  observed <- cor(as.vector(distance), as.vector(cooccurrence),
                  method = "pearson")
  if (!is.finite(observed)) {
    stop("Intergroup Pearson correlation is undefined.")
  }

  set.seed(seed)
  permutation_statistics <- numeric(permutations)
  for (i in seq_len(permutations)) {
    row_permutation <- sample.int(nrow(cooccurrence))
    column_permutation <- sample.int(ncol(cooccurrence))
    permutation_statistics[i] <- cor(
      as.vector(distance),
      as.vector(cooccurrence[row_permutation, column_permutation, drop = FALSE]),
      method = "pearson"
    )
  }
  p_negative <- (sum(permutation_statistics <= observed) + 1) /
    (length(permutation_statistics) + 1)
  list(r = observed, p_negative = p_negative,
       n_pairs = length(distance))
}

intergroup_result <- bipartite_mantel(
  jaccard_cross,
  cooccurrence_cross,
  seed_base + 2L
)

data.frame(
  group = "Lentic-Lotic",
  test = "Pearson correlation, bipartite QAP, one-sided negative",
  r = intergroup_result$r,
  p = intergroup_result$p_negative,
  n_pairs = intergroup_result$n_pairs
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 5)
```

The intergroup analysis is a bipartite QAP-style permutation test, not a classical Mantel test. It correlates only the observed 84 × 35 Lentic–Lotic pairs. Each permutation independently relabels Lentic rows and Lotic columns of the co-occurrence matrix; the same species permutation is applied across every pair involving that species. This preserves the dependence induced by species shared among pairs. The null assumes species labels are exchangeable within each habitat group.

## Results

```{r comparison}
results <- data.frame(
  group = c("Lentic-Lentic", "Lotic-Lotic", "Lentic-Lotic"),
  test = c(
    "Pearson Mantel, one-sided negative",
    "Pearson Mantel, one-sided negative",
    "Pearson correlation, bipartite QAP, one-sided negative"
  ),
  r = c(lentic_result$r, lotic_result$r, intergroup_result$r),
  p = c(lentic_result$p_negative, lotic_result$p_negative,
        intergroup_result$p_negative),
  n_pairs = c(lentic_result$n_pairs, lotic_result$n_pairs,
              intergroup_result$n_pairs),
  n_cells = 2317L,
  permutations = permutations,
  seed = c(seed_base, seed_base + 1L, seed_base + 2L)
)
write.csv(results, file.path(analysis_root, "Mantel_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(results, digits = 5)
```

## Figure 3

```{r figure-3, fig.width=11, fig.height=8, dpi=600}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

within_plot_data <- function(jaccard, cooccurrence) {
  pair_indices <- which(lower.tri(jaccard), arr.ind = TRUE)
  data.frame(
    distance = 1 - jaccard[pair_indices],
    cooccurrence = cooccurrence[pair_indices]
  )
}

plot_group <- function(data, title, method, estimate, p_value, color, line_color) {
  ggplot(data, aes(x = .data$distance, y = .data$cooccurrence)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.55, size = 1.2, color = color) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE,
                color = line_color, linewidth = 1) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = sprintf("%s: r = %.4f; one-sided p = %.4f; n = %s",
                         method, estimate, p_value,
                         format(nrow(data), big.mark = ",")),
      x = "Climatic niche distance (1 - Jaccard)",
      y = "Shared 50-km grid cells"
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.02))) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
      axis.title = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
}

plot_lentic <- plot_group(
  within_plot_data(jaccard_lentic, make_square_cooccurrence(lentic_pairs, lentic_species)),
  "Lentic-Lentic", "Pearson Mantel", lentic_result$r, lentic_result$p_negative,
  "#a6cee3", "#1f78b4"
)
plot_lotic <- plot_group(
  within_plot_data(jaccard_lotic, make_square_cooccurrence(lotic_pairs, lotic_species)),
  "Lotic-Lotic", "Pearson Mantel", lotic_result$r, lotic_result$p_negative,
  "#b2df8a", "#33a02c"
)
plot_intergroup_data <- data.frame(
  distance = as.vector(1 - jaccard_cross),
  cooccurrence = as.vector(cooccurrence_cross)
)
plot_intergroup <- plot_group(
  plot_intergroup_data,
  "Lentic-Lotic", "Bipartite QAP Pearson", intergroup_result$r,
  intergroup_result$p_negative, "#fdbf6f", "#ff7f00"
)

figure_3 <- (plot_lentic | plot_lotic) / plot_intergroup
figure_3
ggsave(
  "04_Figures/Figure_3_niche_cooccurrence.png",
  plot = figure_3,
  width = 11,
  height = 8,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)
```

The regression lines are descriptive least-squares fits; inferential p-values are from the Mantel or bipartite QAP tests indicated in each panel. The absolute number of shared cells can also increase with species range size, so these associations are not interpreted as causal evidence of climatic filtering.
